title: 20-Layer Asymmetric FP with Fixed ±10 nm Perturbation Bounds
scientific_hypothesis: Reducing perturbation amplitude from percentage-based to fixed ±10 nm absolute offsets centered on previously optimized thicknesses will stabilize gradient convergence, prevent thin layers from approaching numerical/fabrication floors, and improve target score beyond 0.9227 while maintaining dual stopband suppression.
design_principle: Asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavity with quarter-wave DBR mirrors and optimized thickness perturbations. Fixed-width offsets preserve intended phase-shift asymmetry while reducing oscillatory weight-shifting between adjacent high/low index pairs.
proposed_topology: Air | [Ta2O5/SiO2]_10 | Fused Silica substrate (20 finite layers total, alternating H/L starting with Ta2O5)
design_variables: All 20 layer thicknesses with ±10 nm bounds centered on baseline thicknesses
manufacturing_considerations: Fixed ±10 nm tolerance bounds support fabrication monitoring
Thicknesses should remain above practical deposition floor (~50 nm)
theory_basis: Defective DBR bandpass filter theory: (HL)^N D(LH)^N structure creates transmission peak at defect wavelength
Quarter-wave optical thickness principle: nH*dH = nL*dL = lambda0/4 for DBR mirrors
Gradient optimization with bounded thickness variables for non-quarter-wave refinement
expected_advantages: Stabilized convergence compared to percentage-based perturbations
Prevents thin layers from approaching fabrication floor
Preserves asymmetric phase-shift mechanism for dual stopband control
Builds directly on verified 0.9227 score baseline
known_risks: Fixed ±10 nm bounds may be too restrictive if baseline thicknesses are far from global optimum
20-layer topology already tested with different thickness combinations (excluded fingerprints)
May not achieve sufficient improvement if asymmetry mechanism is saturated
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 asymmetric Fabry-Perot bandpass filter on Fused Silica substrate with Air incident medium. Layer sequence: Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2 (20 finite layers total, alternating H/L starting with high-index Ta2O5). Initialize thicknesses using baseline values: [157.12, 333.24, 336.89, 284.43, 207.08, 310.49, 120.47, 211.41, 208.75, 286.48, 215.19, 336.73, 157.05, 322.90, 342.41, 254.64, 176.10, 258.47, 182.86, 375.56] nm. Apply optimization bounds of ±10 nm absolute offset from these initial values for each layer (e.g., layer 1: 147.12-167.12 nm, layer 2: 323.24-343.24 nm, etc.). Optimize for maximum transmittance at 1550 nm with strong suppression in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Wavelength range: 1400-1700 nm. Normal incidence (0 degrees). Unpolarized or average of TE/TM. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Transition from percentage-based asymmetric perturbations to fixed ±10 nm absolute offsets centered on baseline optimized thicknesses to prevent thin layers from approaching fabrication floor while preserving phase-shift asymmetry mechanism.
